claims.text: Adding approximately 15% Al2O3 to a TaNbVTi-based refractory high-entropy alloy induces in-situ formation of TiO or similar oxide precipitates.
The Al2O3-induced oxide precipitates are fine and uniformly distributed.
Ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering can process the Al2O3-containing TaNbVTi-based alloy and produce the in-situ TiO-reinforced microstructure.
The oxide precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The Al2O3 addition produces solid-solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening.
The oxide-related strengthening mechanisms remain effective at 1023–1123 K under compressive loading.
The relatively low density of the oxide addition lowers the overall alloy density.
A ductile alloy matrix is responsible for retaining good compressive plasticity.
Approximately 15% Al2O3 will improve high-temperature compressive yield strength by at least 30% relative to material processed without Al2O3.
Approximately 15% Al2O3 will reduce alloy density by about 15% relative to material processed without Al2O3.
The Al2O3-containing alloy will maintain room-temperature ductility comparable to the baseline alloy.
The reported 15% Al2O3 alloy has a compressive yield strength of 1837 MPa and a density of 7.75 g/cm3.
Al2O3 contents beyond the optimized amount may not produce the same beneficial phase formation or mechanical behavior.
Different refractory alloy systems may not exhibit the same phase formation or mechanical response to Al2O3 addition.
The stability and morphology of the in-situ oxides during prolonged high-temperature exposure may vary with processing conditions and alloy composition.
